timeline.message:
Make the attr `new_local_repository.build_file` label-typed

The attribute is string-typed to support a legacy use case where a path instead of a label could be passed. This causes us to parse a passed label as a canonical label, forgoing repo mapping altogether.

Fixes #19963.

RELNOTES[INC]: The attribute `new_local_repository.build_file` no longer accepts a path; a label must be passed instead.
timeline.author: Xùdōng Yáng

timeline.body:
The attribute is string-typed to support a legacy use case where a path instead of a label could be passed. This causes us to parse a passed label as a canonical label, forgoing repo mapping altogether.

Fixes #19963.

RELNOTES[INC]: The attribute `new_local_repository.build_file` no longer accepts a path; a label must be passed instead.
You probably also want to update NewLocalRepositoryFuntion.resolve() because it has a branch for the case where the value of `build_file` is a string.

timeline.body:
Do I understand correctly that this change removes the ability of `new_local_repository` to use BUILD files from an absolute path?

(I think it's a good change per se and that use case looks weird enough that I'd be fine with not having an incompatible flag as long as you do it knowingly)

reply.body: yes indeed. (as the commit message says)

timeline.body:
Why not `WorkspaceAttributeMapper.of(rule).get("build_file", Type.NODEP_LABEL) `?

That seems to be the canonical way to access attributes in the (few) native implementations of workspace rules.

reply.body: I honestly don't think that class needs to exist. Maybe it did at one point but right now it just doesn't do anything. (One extra reason is that WAM.get throws an EvalException which is annoying...)
At least you get a more reasonable exception than `ClassCastException` if you do this. I won't insist, though, it's not a big difference.
thing is, you won't get an exception at all; it's impossible for a label-typed attribute to have a non-label value.
